content.seoTitle: Cherry Blossom Painting Wall Art Prints | Japandi Set of 3
content.metaDescription: Bring calm, Japanese-inspired style to your bedroom with this stunning cherry blossom painting set of 3. Bold Enso ink circles, red blossom tones & waterfall art. Free UK shipping!
content.productDescription:
Bring a real sense of calm into your bedroom with this cherry blossom painting set of three — it's one of those pieces that just makes a room feel more intentional. Each print is centred on a bold, expressive Enso circle rendered in sweeping black ink brushwork, and nestled within that circle sits a different Japanese-inspired scene: a gnarled cherry blossom tree with vivid red-toned blooms, a misty waterfall landscape with dark pine trees and grey rocks, and a second blossom tree with rich red-toned clusters reaching across bare branches. The backgrounds are a clean, soft white, which lets the black ink and those punchy red tones do all the talking.

What I love about this set is how the three prints feel both individual and completely connected. The Enso motif — a brushed circle rooted in Japanese Zen philosophy — ties everything together without making the set feel repetitive. If you want something with quiet strength and a bit of soul for your bedroom walls, this really is it.

What's Included with Cherry Blossom Painting Japandi Enso Circle Ink Art | Set of 3

  • A set of 3 individual art prints, each featuring a unique Japanese Enso ink circle scene in black, white and red tones
  • Printed in the UK using fade-resistant pigment inks for lasting colour — suitable for indoor display
  • Available as unframed prints, or with framed and wrapped canvas options; framed and canvas-wrapped options arrive ready to hang — no hunting for a frame that fits
  • Choose between unframed and framed options in multiple sizes and in Luster or Museum quality; also available in wrapped canvas size options

How to Style cherry blossom painting in a Japandi Bedroom

I'd hang all three in a row at the same height, with an even gap between each — somewhere between 5 and 8 cm usually feels right. Above a bed's headboard is the classic spot, and this set really suits that placement because the soft white backgrounds blend beautifully into light walls without disappearing. The black Enso circles give you that strong visual anchor you need above a large piece of furniture, while the red blossom tones stop the whole thing feeling too stark. For a true Japandi feel, keep the surrounding decor simple: natural wood, linen bedding, maybe a low-profile bedside lamp. This set doesn't need much around it to shine.

If your bedroom walls are a warm greige, soft grey or even a muted sage, these prints will look brilliant. They also work well in a monochrome room where you want one controlled pop of colour — that red is bold but contained, so it never feels out of place. For more Japandi wall art ideas, have a browse through our Japandi wall art collection — there's plenty there to layer with this set.

Choosing the Right Size and Format for Your Space

The first thing I'd think about is the wall space you're working with. If you're hanging above a double or king-size bed, you've got room to go bigger — larger prints let the Enso circles breathe and make more of a statement. For a smaller bedroom or a narrow wall, a medium size still reads beautifully because the composition is so clean and graphic. The white background means even a smaller print holds its own on the wall.

In terms of format, if you want the crispest detail in those ink brushstrokes and the fine texture of the blossom branches, I'd lean towards the Museum quality paper — it really does justice to artwork with this much fine linework. Luster is a lovely option too if you prefer a slightly more vibrant finish. And if you'd rather skip framing entirely and go for something with a bit of texture and depth, the wrapped canvas option is a great shout — it suits the Japandi aesthetic particularly well. Scroll down to see how each size looks in a bedroom before you decide.

aiItems.content:
What is a cherry blossom painting?

A cherry blossom painting is a piece of artwork that depicts the flowering branches of the cherry blossom tree — known in Japan as sakura — and is one of the most enduring motifs in Asian art and culture. These paintings traditionally use ink wash or watercolour techniques to capture the delicate, fleeting beauty of blossom blooms, often set against soft or minimal backgrounds in keeping with Japanese artistic values. In contemporary home decor, cherry blossom paintings are popular for their calming, nature-inspired quality and their versatility — they suit Japandi, minimalist and Asian-inspired interiors especially well. A set of wall art prints featuring cherry blossom scenes is a simple, impactful way to bring that sense of quiet beauty into a bedroom or living space.

How to Hang a Cherry Blossom Painting Set of 3 in a Bedroom

1. Choose your wall: Pick a wall with enough horizontal space for all three prints side by side — above the bed's headboard is the most popular spot, as it creates a natural focal point in the room.

2. Measure and mark: Lay the three prints on the floor first to work out your preferred spacing — a gap of 5 to 8 cm between each print usually looks balanced. Mark the hanging points on the wall with a pencil before putting in any fixings.

3. Hang at eye level: The centre of the prints should sit roughly at eye level when you're standing — for most bedrooms that's around 145 to 155 cm from the floor to the middle of each print. If hanging above a headboard, aim for the bottom of the prints to sit about 15 to 20 cm above the top of the headboard.

4. Check alignment: Use a spirit level across all three prints once they're up — even a slight tilt is really noticeable with a set. Step back and look from the doorway to get the full effect.

5. Style around the prints: Keep the surrounding decor simple to let the Japandi ink artwork breathe — natural textures, neutral bedding and minimal clutter on bedside tables will let the set do the work.

Choosing Your Cherry Blossom Wall Art Print Format

Unframed Print — The print only, ready for you to frame in your own choice of frame. Available on Luster art paper (vibrant, semi-sheen finish) or Museum quality paper (ultra-fine detail, archival standard). Great if you already have a frame or want to match your own decor exactly.

Framed Print — Your chosen print is mounted and framed, arriving completely ready to hang — no sourcing a frame, no hassle. Available in multiple sizes on Luster or Museum quality paper. The most convenient option if you want the set on your wall with minimal effort.

Wrapped Canvas — The artwork is printed directly onto canvas and wrapped around a wooden stretcher frame — no glazing, no frame needed. Has a natural texture that suits the ink-brush style of this Japandi set particularly well. Simply hang straight onto the wall. Available in a range of canvas sizes.

Paper quality: Luster vs Museum — Luster art paper gives a semi-gloss, vibrant finish that makes the black ink and red blossom tones pop. Museum quality paper is the premium archival choice — it captures every fine detail in the brushwork and is made to last for decades without fading. Both are printed with fade-resistant pigment inks in the UK.

aiItems.content:
What are black white photography prints?

Black white photography prints are photographic images reproduced in greyscale — capturing subjects in shades of black, white and grey, without colour. They are printed onto art paper or canvas and sold as wall art for the home, typically in sets that work together as a curated group on your wall. Because they use no colour, they are incredibly versatile and suit almost any room scheme or existing décor. A well-chosen set of black and white photography prints can add real depth, mood and visual interest to a bedroom, living room or hallway without clashing with anything you already have.

How to Hang Black White Photography Prints as a Set of 3

1. Choose your wall and measure up: Find a wall with enough width for all three prints side by side — ideally at least 1.5 times the combined width of the prints. Above a bed or sofa is a classic starting point.

2. Mark the centre point: Find the centre of your wall space and work outward from there so the set sits symmetrically. Use a pencil mark at the height you want the top of the prints to sit.

3. Keep gaps even: Aim for a gap of around 5–8 cm between each print — close enough to read as a set, far enough apart that each image has room to breathe.

4. Use a spirit level: Even a small tilt is very noticeable across a run of three prints. A small spirit level (or the level tool on your phone) takes seconds and saves a lot of straightening later.

5. Step back and check before you fix: Hold the prints up against the wall or use paper templates cut to size — it's much easier to adjust the position before you put holes in the wall.

Unframed, Framed or Canvas — Which Option Is Right for You?

Arrives ready to hang — Unframed print: No. Framed print: Yes. Wrapped canvas: Yes.

Frame included — Unframed print: No (you choose your own). Framed print: Yes. Wrapped canvas: No frame needed.

Best for — Unframed print: Those who want to choose their own frame or already have one. Framed print: Quickest, most convenient — perfect if you want everything done for you. Wrapped canvas: A chunkier, contemporary look with real texture and no frame required.

Finish feel — Unframed print: Flat, lightweight, flexible. Framed print: Polished, gallery-ready. Wrapped canvas: Textural, three-dimensional, modern.

aiItems.content:
What are black white photography prints?

Black white photography prints are art prints made from real photographic images captured in monochrome, reproducing scenes from nature, landscape, wildlife or architecture using only black, white and grey tones. They are printed onto quality art paper or canvas using fade-resistant pigment inks, giving you a crisp, long-lasting image that suits a wide range of interior styles. Because they contain no colour, black and white photography prints are incredibly versatile — they work with almost any wall colour and blend easily with existing furniture and decor. They are a popular choice for bedrooms, living rooms and hallways where a calm, timeless atmosphere is wanted. A set of 3 prints displayed together creates a gallery-style statement wall with real visual impact.

How to Hang Black White Photography Prints as a Set of 3

1. Measure your wall space: Hold a tape measure across the wall where you plan to hang the prints and note the total width available. For a set of 3, allow roughly equal space for each print plus a consistent gap of 5–8 cm between each one so the set reads as a unified display.

2. Mark your positions before you hang: Cut three pieces of paper to the size of the prints you have ordered and use low-tack tape to fix them to the wall first. Step back and check the arrangement looks balanced before you make any holes — it saves a lot of bother later.

3. Hang at the right height: The centre of the middle print should sit roughly at eye level, which for most people is around 145–150 cm from the floor. If you are hanging the set above a bed or a piece of furniture, position the bottom edge of the prints about 20–25 cm above the furniture top.

4. Keep spacing consistent: Use a small ruler or a piece of card cut to your chosen gap width as a spacer when you hang each print — this makes it much easier to get perfectly even gaps without measuring every time.

5. Step back and adjust: Once all three are up, stand back from a distance to check everything is level and evenly spaced. A spirit level app on your phone works brilliantly for this final check.

aiItems.content:
What are pictures for the bedroom wall?

Pictures for the bedroom wall are art prints or framed artworks chosen specifically to hang in a bedroom, creating atmosphere, adding colour and personality, and turning a plain wall into a focal point. They range from single statement pieces to coordinated sets — like a triptych of Scandinavian landscape prints — that work together to give the room a unified look and feel. The best bedroom wall art tends to use calmer, more restful tones and subjects than pieces chosen for busier living spaces, helping the room feel like a genuine sanctuary. Sets of three are particularly popular because they fill a wall above a bed naturally and look considered without requiring any additional styling effort.

How to Hang Pictures for the Bedroom Wall: A Simple Step-by-Step Guide

1. Choose your wall and measure up: Decide which wall you want to use — above the bed is the most popular spot. Measure the width of the bed or headboard, then aim for your set of prints to span roughly two-thirds of that width for a balanced, well-proportioned look.

2. Pick your size before you order: Use the size guide image on the product page to see how each size looks in a real bedroom. For most double or king-size beds, a medium or large size works best. For a single bed or side wall, a smaller size usually fits more comfortably.

3. Mark your hanging points: Hold the centre print up to the wall at the height you want — generally around 15–20 cm above the headboard — and mark the hanging point lightly with a pencil. Then mark the two outer prints, keeping an even gap (around 4–6 cm) between each frame.

4. Hang from the centre outwards: Always hang the centre print first, check it's level, then hang the left and right prints to match. A spirit level or the spirit level app on your phone makes this much easier and takes just a minute.

5. Step back and adjust: Once all three are up, step back to the doorway and check the arrangement from a distance. Small tweaks are much easier to spot from across the room than when you're standing close to the wall.

Unframed, Framed or Wrapped Canvas — Which Option Is Right for You?

Arrives ready to hang — Unframed print: No, you will need to source your own frame. Framed print: Yes, hang it straight out of the packaging. Wrapped canvas: Yes, ready to hang immediately.

Paper / material — Unframed print: Luster art paper or Museum quality paper, your choice. Framed print: Luster art paper or Museum quality paper, your choice. Wrapped canvas: Art printed directly onto canvas and wrapped around a wooden frame.

Finish look — Unframed print: Crisp, flat print — great if you want to choose your own frame style. Framed print: Clean, gallery-ready look with a neat border. Wrapped canvas: Textured, tactile feel with a contemporary edge — no frame needed.

Best for — Unframed print: Buyers who already have frames or want a specific frame colour or style. Framed print: Anyone who wants a polished, cohesive result without the effort of framing. Wrapped canvas: Those who prefer a modern, borderless look with a bit of depth and texture.

aiItems.content:
What is landscape art?

Landscape art is artwork that depicts natural outdoor scenes — mountains, forests, coastlines, valleys and skies — as its primary subject. It is one of the oldest and most enduring genres in art history, spanning everything from classical oil paintings to modern minimalist prints. Today, landscape art wall art prints are particularly popular in home interiors because they bring a sense of space, calm and the natural world into any room. Scandi and Nordic-style landscape art, in particular, has become a go-to choice for bedrooms and living rooms where a peaceful, pared-back atmosphere is the goal.

How to Hang a Set of 3 Landscape Art Prints in Your Bedroom

1. Choose your wall: Pick a wall with enough width to display all three prints side by side comfortably — above a headboard or along a main bedroom wall both work brilliantly for a set of 3.

2. Plan your spacing: Lay the prints out on the floor first to check the overall width. Aim for an even gap of around 3–5 cm between each print so they read as a cohesive set rather than three separate pieces.

3. Find your height: The centre of your arrangement should sit roughly at eye level when you are standing — for above a bed, aim for the bottom edge of the prints to sit around 15–20 cm above the headboard.

4. Mark and hang: Use a spirit level and a pencil to mark your hanging points before you put any nails in the wall. Starting with the centre print and working outward keeps everything symmetrical.

5. Step back and adjust: Once all three are up, step back and view from the doorway. Small adjustments at this stage are much easier than after you've admired them for a week!

Which Option Is Right for You? Comparing Your Choices

Unframed Print on Luster Paper — A great choice if you already have frames you love or want full control over your framing style. Luster paper gives a gentle sheen that keeps whites bright — perfect for this white and grey mountain artwork. You'll need to source and fit your own frames.

Unframed Print on Museum Quality Paper — The premium unframed option. Museum quality paper delivers deeper contrast and a fine-art feel that really brings out the painterly texture in these mountain scenes. Again, framing is down to you.

Framed Print (Luster or Museum Paper) — Your prints arrive ready to hang straight away — no frame hunting required. A brilliant time-saver and the finish is consistently smart. Choose your preferred paper quality at checkout.

Wrapped Canvas — Printed onto canvas and stretched over a wooden frame, this option has a tactile, gallery-style quality that suits the painterly style of this mountain artwork especially well. Arrives ready to hang with no frame needed.

aiItems.content:
What are landscape wall art prints?

Landscape wall art prints are printed artworks depicting natural scenes — mountains, forests, coastlines, open skies — designed to be displayed on your walls at home. They come in a range of formats including unframed prints, framed prints and wrapped canvas, so you can choose what suits your space and budget. This set of 3 Scandinavian snow mountain prints is a great example: three cohesive pieces that work together to create a calm, Nordic atmosphere in a bedroom or living space. Landscape prints are one of the most popular choices for UK homes because they bring a sense of the outdoors in and suit almost every decorating style, from Scandi-minimal to contemporary classic.

How to Hang a Set of 3 Landscape Wall Art Prints

1. Choose your wall: Pick a wide, clear wall with enough room for all three prints side by side — above a bed or along a hallway works really well for a set of 3. Measure the total width you have available before you choose your print size.

2. Plan your layout: Lay the prints out on the floor first to check the arrangement and spacing. For a set of 3, a straight horizontal row at the same height is the most popular and effective layout. Aim for a gap of around 5–8 cm between each print.

3. Mark your fixing points: Use a spirit level and a pencil to mark where each hook or nail will go. Measure up from the floor (or down from the ceiling) rather than eyeballing it — a level line makes all the difference to the finished look.

4. Hang and check: Hang the centre print first, then work outwards to the left and right. Step back after each one and check the alignment before you commit. Adjust as needed — it's worth taking the extra minute.

5. Style around the art: Once your prints are up, bring in soft furnishings, lighting or accessories that pick up on the colours in the artwork. For this Nordic snow mountain set, cool greys, whites and navy blues in cushions, throws or a rug all complement the palette beautifully.

Choosing Your Landscape Wall Art Print Format

Format — Unframed Print. The print is delivered rolled or flat, ready for you to frame yourself. Perfect if you already have a frame or want full control over the finish.

Format — Framed Print. Arrives ready to hang straight out of the box — no extra shopping, no hassle. A great choice if you want a complete, polished look with no effort.

Format — Wrapped Canvas. The artwork is printed directly onto canvas and stretched over a wooden frame, with the image wrapping around the edges. Ready to hang and gives a contemporary, frameless feel.

Paper quality (prints only) — Luster Art Paper. A semi-gloss finish that makes colours pop and works well in rooms with natural light. Durable and vibrant.

Paper quality (prints only) — Museum Quality Paper. A fine-art matte finish that gives a softer, more considered look — especially lovely in a bedroom or lower-light space. The premium choice for a gallery-quality result.
